text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary function tests (PFTs) are a group of tests that measure how well your lungs work. They are often used to help diagnose and monitor asthma, a condition where the airways narrow and swell, making it difficult to breathe. PFTs can help determine if there is airway obstruction, how severe it is, and whether it's reversible with medication.
snippet_highlighted_words: a group of tests that measure how well your lungs work

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: PFTs, particularly spirometry, can help identify airway obstruction, a key characteristic of asthma.

list.title: Assessing Severity:
list.snippet: PFTs can show how severe the airway obstruction is by measuring parameters like FEV1 (forced expiratory volume in one second).

list.title: Monitoring:
list.snippet: PFTs can track how well asthma is controlled over time and how well patients respond to treatment.

list.title: Reversibility:
list.snippet: PFTs can assess the reversibility of airway obstruction by measuring how much the FEV1 improves after using a bronchodilator like albuterol.
